newsitem.title: UK: Dana to take hefty charge with Europe sale.
newsitem.headline: Dana to take hefty charge with Europe sale.

text.p: Dana Corporation of the U.S. said on Thursday the planned sale of its European warehouse distribution operations to Britain's Partco Group Plc would result in an after-tax profit of about $47 million but the bulk of this would be used to restructure a French business.

In a statement issued in London, Dana said the 103 million stg sale of its European operation -- the largest divestment in its history -- would allow it to rationalise its Perfect Circle Europe operations in France.
"This transaction will benefit both Dana and the operations it is divesting," chairman Southwood J Morcott was quoted as saying.
He said it allowed the company to concentrate its resources on maximising growth oppportunities in its core businesses and continue to distribute its manufactured products globally.
"Dana is primarily a vehicular components manufacturing company and not a warehouse distributor," Morcott said.

The group's plans for Perfect Circle include seeking to sell its piston manufacturing facility in Liancourt, reorganising its Dreux piston ring machining operation and downsizing and moving its Poissy division office.
Dana's British paints and finishing products chain Brown Brothers, with 135 distribution points, forms the bulk of assets in the sale.
